procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at home in Granby, consented to telehealth. Roads were bad this week so he asked to do this one by video.

Labs from 3/13 reviewed with him: A1c about the same as December, still over 9. Creatinine unchanged, potassium normal.

He reads off his log: fasting 150s-190s, pre-dinner often 200+. Has been taking lispro at dinner more consistently since New Year's. No hypoglycemia. Knee stiff in the cold mornings, loosens up after he gets moving. No new symptoms.

A/P
T2DM, still poorly controlled. Glargine 30 at bedtime, lispro sliding scale, no change. Encouraged him to keep the dinner dose habit going.
CKD 3a, HTN: stable labs, continue lisinopril 10. Home BP readings he reports sound fine.
OA L knee: acetaminophen as needed.
In-person visit in June. Due for eye exam in May.

documents.title: Optometry Report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Annual diabetic eye exam, seen 06/05/2025.
Allergies: NKDA.
VA cc 20/25 each eye. Pupils equal and reactive. Pressures normal. Dilated exam: optic nerves healthy, maculae flat, no hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization. No diabetic retinopathy OU.
Return 1 year. Copy to primary care. — Optometry

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: f/u DM, CKD, HTN.

HPI: rescheduled from June. Says the spring was 'not great' for his sugars. Morning readings 180-230 on the meter download, some evening values in the 250s. Missing lispro at lunch most days and at dinner a couple times a week. Glargine every night. No lows, no polyuria he's noticed. Knee: same aching, worse after mowing, Tylenol helps. Eye exam 6/5: no retinopathy.

Meds: glargine 30 u qhs, lispro SSI AC, lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 40, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: NAD. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Ext no edema. Feet intact skin, sensation intact to monofilament.

Data: A1c today higher than March, mid-9s. Creatinine at his usual, K ok.

A/P
1. T2DM, poorly controlled, A1c up. Long talk again about mealtime insulin. He is willing to set phone alarms for lunch and dinner doses. Same regimen.
2. CKD 3a: stable. Lisinopril continues. Avoid NSAIDs.
3. HTN: continue.
4. OA L knee: stable on acetaminophen.
Physical in September.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual preventive visit. 64 y/o man, turns 65 in December.

Since last visit: no illnesses, no ED. The phone alarms worked for about a month, then he stopped. Morning sugars 170s-200s. Walking less this summer because of the knee and the heat. Tylenol two or three times a week. Mood fine, PHQ-9 low. Drinks a beer on weekends.

Meds reconciled, unchanged. NKDA.

Exam: Alert, comfortable. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes, thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, nontender, no bruit, no pulsatile mass. Ext warm, no edema. L knee: crepitus and bony change, no effusion or warmth. Feet: skin intact, nails ok, monofilament normal bilaterally, DP/PT palpable. Skin unremarkable.

Assessment and plan
- T2DM, poorly controlled: A1c drawn. He is not interested in adding anything today; continue glargine 30 u qhs and lispro per scale.
- CKD 3a: CMP, UACR. Lisinopril 10.
- HTN: continue.
- Statin: lipid panel, atorvastatin 40.
- L knee OA: acetaminophen.
- Prevention: flu shot today. COVID booster at pharmacy. Yearly LDCT ordered. Colonoscopy due 2029. Eye exam current. Tdap 2024, Shingrix and RSV done, PCV20 done.
- Medicare starts in December; book the Welcome to Medicare visit early in the new year.
f/u January.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stan, A1c is still in the 9s, a little lower than July but not where it needs to be. Kidney function unchanged from prior years, and the urine protein test is still normal. Cholesterol and blood counts fine, liver tests normal. Let's keep working on the mealtime doses and revisit in January.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
CLINICAL HISTORY: Lung cancer screening, annual. Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 2018.
TECHNIQUE: Low-dose CT of the chest without contrast.
COMPARISON: 10/22/2024 and 10/17/2023.
FINDINGS: No lung nodules. No airspace disease, no effusion, no pneumothorax. No enlarged lymph nodes. Normal heart size, no pericardial effusion. Limited upper abdomen normal.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS category 1: negative. Recommend annual LDCT.

documents.title: LDCT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Third negative annual screen, Lung-RADS 1. Pt notified via portal. Next due 10/2026.
